data.title: Insufficient Logging and Detection Coverage
data.summary: Activity performed during testing — credential attacks, lateral movement, privilege escalation and data access — produced no alert and in several cases no retained log at all, so the same activity by an attacker would not have been noticed.
data.description:
Detection is what bounds the damage of a compromise. Prevention fails eventually; whether that failure becomes an incident or a breach depends on whether anyone notices.

The gap is usually not the absence of logs but their fate: logs stay on the host that produced them, where an attacker with administrative access can clear them; retention is too short to investigate a compromise that began weeks earlier; or the events are collected but no rule turns them into an alert anyone sees.

A test is the cheapest opportunity to measure this. The activity is known, timed and documented, so it can be compared directly against what the defenders saw — and the answer is routinely "nothing".
data.recommendation:
* Centralise logs off the hosts that generate them, with retention long enough to investigate — a year for authentication and administrative activity.
* Collect the sources that matter: authentication, process creation with command lines, PowerShell, DNS, EDR telemetry, and cloud audit logs.
* Write and test detections for the techniques this assessment used, and verify them by re-running the activity.
* Confirm alerts reach somebody who acts, with a defined response path out of hours.
data.short_recommendation: Centralise logs and alert on the techniques used against you.

attack_techniques.technique: T1685.002 — Disable or Modify Cloud Log
